intent.raw_query: Vancouver food and nature, $1800 solo, 4 days, June 2027, from Seattle

experiences.name: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Granville Island Public Market, sampling local artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, handmade pastries, and BC wines. Chat with local vendors and discover the best of Vancouver's culinary scene in one iconic waterfront location.

Explore scenic trails along rushing waterfalls and pools, with stops at the Ecology Centre to learn about the local rainforest ecosystem. A stunning and budget-friendly alternative to Capilano.

Sample har gow, BBQ pork buns, and egg tarts at legendary local spots, and explore the Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden nearby.

experiences.name: Grouse Mountain Hike & Wildlife Refuge

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Vancouver International Airport at 12:00 PM on Flight AC. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Canada Line SkyTrain directly from YVR to downtown Vancouver — a budget-friendly option at ~$4 CAD. Check in to Vancouver Harbour Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Granville Island Public Market Food Tour. Explore the vibrant market stalls sampling local artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, baked goods, and seasonal produce. This is a great low-cost way to graze on local food and soak up the atmosphere without a big spend. Walk across the Granville Bridge or take the mini False Creek Ferry (~$4 CAD) to reach the island.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the False Creek seawall back toward downtown as the sun sets over the harbour. Grab a casual dinner at one of the food trucks or affordable eateries near Yaletown. Rest up after a travel day.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or during your flight — skip or grab a coffee and snack at YVR arrivals.
meals.lunch: Graze the Granville Island Public Market stalls — budget $10–15 CAD on samples of local cheeses, smoked salmon, and fresh bread.
meals.dinner: Yaletown food trucks or Robson Street casual spots — try Japadog (Japanese-style hot dogs, ~$8–12 CAD) or a slice from Nat's New York Pizzeria (~$5–7 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Canada Line SkyTrain from YVR to downtown costs ~$4 CAD with a Compass Card (purchase at the airport). Granville Island Market is free to enter — budget $10–20 CAD for food sampling. Keep Day 1 light given travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with the Chinatown Night Market & Dim Sum Experience. Head to Vancouver's historic Chinatown for an authentic dim sum brunch at one of the neighbourhood's classic, budget-friendly restaurants. Dishes are typically $3–6 CAD per plate. Explore the Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden (free outer garden) and the colourful Chinatown streets afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus ride to Stanley Park. Begin the Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Nature Walk — rent a bike from Spokes Bicycle Rentals near the park entrance (~$8–12 CAD/hour) and ride the iconic 10km seawall. Pass ancient cedar forests, totem poles, Siwash Rock, and stunning views of the North Shore mountains and harbour. Lock up the bike and walk the forest trails if time allows.
day_by_day.evening: Return bikes and wind down with a picnic or takeaway meal near English Bay Beach. Watch the sunset over the Pacific from the beach — one of Vancouver's best free experiences. Head back to the hotel via bus.

meals.breakfast: Grab a steamed bun or congee from a Chinatown bakery before dim sum — ~$2–4 CAD.
meals.lunch: Dim sum brunch in Chinatown at New Town Bakery or Pink Pearl — budget $12–18 CAD per person for a satisfying spread.
meals.dinner: Picnic at English Bay — pick up affordable groceries or takeaway from a nearby deli or Safeway (~$8–12 CAD). Alternatively, try a bowl from Pho Bich Nga in Chinatown (~$12 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Chinatown is easily reachable by bus (Routes 3 or 8 from downtown). Stanley Park bike rentals are first-come, first-served — arrive by early afternoon on weekdays to avoid queues. Seawall is free to walk/cycle. English Bay sunset is a must-do free activity.

day_by_day.morning: Take TransLink bus to Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre — a completely free alternative to the famous Capilano Suspension Bridge. Cross the thrilling suspension bridge over Lynn Canyon, explore old-growth forest trails, and visit the free Ecology Centre to learn about the local rainforest ecosystem. The 30-minute bus journey from downtown costs ~$3.15 CAD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking Lynn Canyon's trail network — the Twin Falls Trail and Rice Lake Loop are scenic, well-marked, and free. Pack a lunch to enjoy creekside in the forest. Return to Vancouver by mid-afternoon via bus.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Commercial Drive neighbourhood (known locally as 'The Drive') — Vancouver's bohemian, multicultural street lined with independent cafes, street art, and affordable international eateries. Browse local shops and enjoy the laid-back local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal or toast at the hotel, or grab a coffee and muffin from a local café near the hotel (~$5–7 CAD).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a nearby grocery store before heading to Lynn Canyon — sandwiches, fruit, and snacks for ~$8–10 CAD. Eat creekside in the forest.
meals.dinner: Commercial Drive offers excellent budget dining — try La Taqueria for tacos (~$4–5 CAD each) or Havana Restaurant for affordable Cuban-inspired dishes (~$14–18 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Lynn Canyon is entirely free — no admission fees for the bridge or trails. Take Bus 228 from Lonsdale Quay (reached via SeaBus from Waterfront Station, ~$3.15 CAD). Wear sturdy shoes and bring water. Commercial Drive is reachable by SkyTrain (Broadway-City Hall) or bus.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Granville Island for a final leisurely morning — pick up any last local food souvenirs (smoked salmon, local honey, artisan jams) at the Public Market. These make great budget-friendly gifts. Wander the artisan studios and Net Loft boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the South False Creek Seawall from Granville Island toward Olympic Village — a scenic, free route with public art installations and great city views. Stop at the Olympic Village plaza and grab a coffee at 49th Parallel Coffee Roasters, one of Vancouver's beloved local roasters. Spend remaining time exploring the neighbourhood or heading back to the hotel to pack.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Vancouver — treat yourself to a slightly elevated but still budget-conscious meal. Head to Robson Street or Davie Village for a satisfying send-off dinner. Pack bags and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastry and coffee from the Granville Island Public Market bakery stalls — ~$6–9 CAD.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Olympic Village — grab a banh mi from a nearby Vietnamese spot or a bowl from Tap & Barrel's happy hour menu (~$10–14 CAD).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at The Naam (Vancouver's oldest vegetarian restaurant, affordable and beloved) or Ramen Danbo for a hearty bowl of ramen (~$13–16 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late departure. Granville Island artisan food products make excellent, locally sourced souvenirs at reasonable prices. The False Creek Seawall walk is completely free and takes about 45–60 minutes at a leisurely pace.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight AC arrives at 12:00 PM. Allow time for deplaning, baggage claim, and transit to Vancouver Harbour Stay (approximately 30–45 minutes by SkyTrain or taxi).
day_by_day.afternoon: After checking in and freshening up, take a leisurely stroll along the Vancouver Harbour waterfront. Explore Canada Place, enjoy views of the North Shore mountains, and get oriented with the city. Stop by the Vancouver Visitor Centre for maps and tips.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gastown, Vancouver's oldest neighbourhood (walkable from the harbour area). Browse the cobblestone streets, see the famous Steam Clock, and settle in for a relaxed first dinner at a local gastropub or casual eatery.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and snack on the plane or at YVR airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick, satisfying bite near the hotel — try Noodle Box or a nearby café for a fast, flavourful mid-range meal around $15–20 CAD.
meals.dinner: Meat & Bread (Gastown) — renowned for their porchetta sandwich and local craft beer. Casual, mid-range, around $20–30 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance (standard is 3:00 PM — ask about early check-in). Pack comfortable walking shoes for the evening stroll. Gastown is approximately 10–15 minutes on foot from the harbour area.

day_by_day.morning: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour — Head to Granville Island (20-minute bus or False Creek ferry from downtown) and spend the morning exploring the vibrant public market. Sample local artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, handmade pastries, and seasonal BC produce. Chat with vendors and soak in the bustling market atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Nature Walk — Rent a bike from Spokes Bicycle Rentals near the park entrance (approximately $10–15/hour CAD) and ride the iconic 10km seawall loop. Pass through ancient cedar forests, take in views of Lions Gate Bridge, visit Siwash Rock, and stop at Prospect Point for panoramic mountain and ocean vistas. Lock up the bike and take a short nature walk through the forest trails.
day_by_day.evening: Return bikes and head to Robson Street or Davie Village for dinner. Explore the lively neighbourhood atmosphere before settling in for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Start at the hotel or grab fresh pastries and a coffee from Terra Breads inside Granville Island Market — a local favourite, around $10–15 CAD.
meals.lunch: Eat at Granville Island Market itself — pick up fresh Dungeness crab, chowder, or a gourmet sandwich from the market stalls. Budget $15–25 CAD for a generous spread.
meals.dinner: The Teahouse in Stanley Park — a mid-range restaurant with beautiful ocean views and Pacific Northwest cuisine. Mains around $25–40 CAD. Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Check the False Creek ferry schedule for a scenic and practical route to Granville Island (runs frequently, ~$5–7 CAD each way). Start the seawall ride before 2:00 PM to avoid afternoon crowds. Bike rentals are first-come, first-served on weekends — arrive early.

day_by_day.morning: Grouse Mountain Hike & Wildlife Refuge — Take the SeaBus to North Vancouver, then bus #236 to the Grouse Mountain base (approximately 45 minutes total). Tackle the legendary Grouse Grind — a challenging 2.9km climb through dense BC forest with 853m of elevation gain. At the summit, visit the Wildlife Refuge to see rescued grizzly bears and grey wolves in their habitat. Enjoy sweeping views over Vancouver and the Strait of Georgia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre — After descending Grouse Mountain (take the gondola down, included with Grind ticket), head to Lynn Canyon Park by bus (approximately 20 minutes). Cross the free suspension bridge over the dramatic Lynn Canyon gorge, hike scenic forest trails, and visit the Ecology Centre to learn about the old-growth ecosystem. A quieter, free alternative to Capilano.
day_by_day.evening: Return to downtown Vancouver via North Vancouver transit. Spend the evening exploring the Chinatown neighbourhood at a relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: Fuel up before the hike — eat at the hotel or stop at Waves Coffee House near the SeaBus terminal for eggs, toast, and coffee. Around $12–18 CAD.
meals.lunch: Pack trail snacks (energy bars, fruit, nuts) for the Grouse Grind. At the summit, grab a casual bite at the Altitudes Bistro — soups, sandwiches, and mountain views. Around $18–25 CAD.
meals.dinner: Phnom Penh Restaurant in Chinatown — a Vancouver institution famous for butter beef and garlic prawns. Vibrant atmosphere, mid-range pricing around $20–30 CAD per person. Expect a short wait — worth it.

day_by_day.notes: The Grouse Grind is strenuous — wear proper hiking shoes and bring at least 1.5L of water per person. The Grind is typically open June through October, weather permitting. Gondola descent costs approximately $15 CAD. Lynn Canyon is free to enter — a great budget-friendly add-on. Allow 3–4 hours total for the Grind and summit activities.

day_by_day.morning: Chinatown Night Market & Dim Sum Experience — Begin your final morning with an authentic dim sum brunch in Vancouver's historic Chinatown. Enjoy classic dishes like har gow, siu mai, egg tarts, and cheung fun in a traditional tea house setting. After brunch, wander through Chinatown's colourful streets, visit the Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden, and browse local shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon doing any last-minute shopping or sightseeing. Visit Robson Street for souvenirs, explore Yaletown's boutiques and waterfront, or return to a favourite spot from earlier in the trip. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell dinner at a mid-range Vancouver restaurant showcasing the best of the city's multicultural food scene before heading to the airport or winding down at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Light continental breakfast at the hotel to save appetite for dim sum.
meals.lunch: Dim sum brunch at Kirin Seafood Restaurant or The Boss Bakery & Restaurant in Chinatown — a classic Vancouver experience. Budget $20–35 CAD per person for a full spread of dishes.
meals.dinner: Miku Restaurant — celebrated for its flame-seared Aburi sushi and West Coast Japanese cuisine. A special farewell splurge, mains around $30–50 CAD. Located near the harbour for a scenic final meal with waterfront views.

day_by_day.notes: Dim sum is typically served until 2:30–3:00 PM — arrive by 11:00 AM to avoid long waits on weekends. The Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Garden charges a small admission (~$14 CAD) but is beautifully serene. Confirm hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure is in the evening. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours to reach YVR by transit from downtown.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Vancouver International Airport at 12:00 PM on Flight AC. Private luxury transfer arranged to Vancouver Harbour Stay. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your premium harbour-view suite. Take a leisurely orientation stroll along the waterfront promenade to get your bearings and soak in the stunning views of Burrard Inlet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour — just a short scenic taxi or water taxi ride from the harbour. Explore the vibrant market sampling local artisan cheeses, freshly shucked Pacific oysters, house-made charcuterie, wild salmon, and artisan pastries. Engage with local vendors and pick up premium provisions for your room.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a top waterfront restaurant near the hotel — recommended: Blue Water Cafe in Yaletown, celebrated for its world-class raw bar and sustainably sourced Pacific seafood. Enjoy Dungeness crab, BC spot prawns, and an expertly curated BC wine list. After dinner, a relaxed night cap at the hotel bar with panoramic harbour views.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival. Grab a light bite at the airport lounge or enjoy complimentary welcome amenities at the hotel upon check-in.
meals.lunch: Granville Island Public Market food tour serves as a premium grazing lunch — highlights include fresh oysters, smoked wild salmon, artisan breads, aged local cheeses, and handcrafted chocolates.
meals.dinner: Blue Water Cafe & Raw Bar, Yaletown — one of Vancouver's most acclaimed seafood restaurants. Budget approximately CAD $180–$250 per person with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through the hotel concierge. Request a harbour-view suite on a high floor for the best arrival experience. Water taxi from Granville Island back to the waterfront is a scenic and enjoyable option in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Nature Walk — rent premium e-bikes or classic bikes from a concierge-arranged provider near the hotel. Ride the iconic 10 km seawall around Stanley Park, passing ancient cedar forests, totem poles, Siwash Rock, and sweeping views of the North Shore mountains and Lions Gate Bridge. Stop at Prospect Point for panoramic photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the seawall, enjoy a leisurely walk through Stanley Park's interior old-growth forest trails. Visit the Vancouver Aquarium within the park (optional premium add-on). Return to the hotel mid-afternoon for a spa treatment or pool time — book the hotel spa for a signature West Coast-inspired massage or body treatment to recover from the morning activity.
day_by_day.evening: Chinatown Night Market & Dim Sum Experience — explore Vancouver's historic Chinatown neighbourhood in the early evening. Stroll the night market for street snacks and local culture, then transition to a premium dinner at Mott 32 Vancouver, an award-winning modern Chinese restaurant offering elevated Cantonese cuisine with exceptional cocktails and an impressive wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at the Vancouver Harbour Stay — opt for the full à la carte premium breakfast featuring eggs Benedict with smoked BC salmon, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee. Budget CAD $40–$60 per person.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch at Stanley Park — have the hotel concierge arrange a premium packed lunch with artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, BC fruit, and sparkling water, enjoyed at Second Beach or Prospect Point with mountain views.
meals.dinner: Mott 32 Vancouver, Chinatown — renowned for Peking duck, dim sum classics elevated to fine dining, and exceptional cocktails. Budget approximately CAD $150–$200 per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Book bike rentals the evening before through the hotel concierge to ensure premium equipment availability. The seawall is best enjoyed in the morning before afternoon crowds build. Spa treatments at the hotel should be booked 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Grouse Mountain Hike & Wildlife Refuge — arrange a private transfer to the Grouse Mountain base. Take on the legendary Grouse Grind trail, a 2.9 km intense climb through dense BC coastal forest with an 853 m elevation gain. At the summit, visit the Wildlife Refuge to see grizzly bears and grey wolves in their natural habitat setting, and enjoy breathtaking 360-degree views over Vancouver and the Lower Mainland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy lunch at The Observatory at Grouse Mountain — one of Vancouver's most spectacular fine dining venues perched at the summit. After lunch, explore the mountaintop attractions including the lumberjack show, birds of prey demonstrations, and scenic chairlift rides. Take the gondola back down for a comfortable descent. Return to the hotel for a rest and refresh.
day_by_day.evening: Premium dinner at Hawksworth Restaurant in the Rosewood Hotel Georgia — consistently ranked among Canada's best restaurants. Chef David Hawksworth's contemporary Canadian cuisine showcases the finest BC ingredients including wild game, foraged mushrooms, and Pacific seafood. Pair with selections from their extraordinary 1,000-label wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before the hike — protein-focused with eggs, smoked salmon, yogurt, and fresh fruit to fuel the Grouse Grind climb.
meals.lunch: The Observatory Restaurant at Grouse Mountain — elevated Canadian cuisine at the summit with panoramic views. Highlights include BC charcuterie boards, wild salmon, and locally inspired seasonal dishes. Budget CAD $80–$120 per person.
meals.dinner: Hawksworth Restaurant, downtown Vancouver — tasting menu recommended at approximately CAD $175–$225 per person, with optional wine pairing at CAD $95–$130 additional.

day_by_day.notes: The Grouse Grind is a strenuous hike — wear proper trail shoes and bring water. The hotel concierge can arrange a private guide if preferred. Note that the Grouse Grind descent is not permitted on foot — the gondola must be taken down (ticket required, approximately CAD $15). Book The Observatory and Hawksworth Restaurant reservations well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre — arrange a private luxury transfer to North Vancouver for a final immersive nature experience. Hike through stunning old-growth forest and cross the dramatic free suspension bridge over Lynn Canyon. Explore the Ecology Centre to learn about the unique BC rainforest ecosystem. Enjoy multiple scenic viewpoints, waterfalls, and swimming holes along the canyon trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Vancouver and spend the final afternoon indulging in a premium shopping experience on Robson Street or at Pacific Centre for high-end souvenirs and local luxury goods. Alternatively, visit the Museum of Anthropology at UBC for world-class First Nations art and cultural artifacts — a profound and memorable final cultural experience. Return to the hotel for final packing and checkout formalities.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Botanist Restaurant at the Fairmont Pacific Rim — an extraordinary celebration of Pacific Northwest botanicals and ingredients. The stunning bar and garden-inspired dining room make it one of Vancouver's most beautiful restaurants. Enjoy their signature tasting menu with BC wine or craft cocktail pairing before a private luxury transfer to the airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Final leisurely in-hotel breakfast — order the full premium spread including eggs any style, smoked BC wild salmon Benedict, house-made pastries, fresh-pressed juices, and premium coffee. A relaxed and indulgent send-off meal.
meals.lunch: Casual premium lunch at The Lobby Lounge at the Fairmont Pacific Rim or a chef's table experience at a local Lonsdale Quay restaurant in North Vancouver after Lynn Canyon — fresh seafood chowder, BC crab cakes, and locally brewed craft beer or sparkling wine. Budget CAD $60–$90 per person.
meals.dinner: Botanist Restaurant, Fairmont Pacific Rim — tasting menu at approximately CAD $165–$210 per person with beverage pairing. One of Vancouver's most celebrated and visually stunning dining experiences — a perfect farewell to the city.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange luggage storage if your departure flight is late evening. Lynn Canyon is a free attraction — no admission fee for the suspension bridge, making it an authentic and unspoiled alternative to the more commercial Capilano Suspension Bridge. Book farewell dinner at Botanist at least 48–72 hours in advance as it is highly sought after. Arrange private airport transfer for departure through the hotel concierge.
